result.summary: The audit is written to audit_2.yaml. Slots a and b and R group 1 are word for word the same as the first draft (corr_1 and corr_2 differ only in the three R-2 rows). I re-checked them and the outcome stands. Slot a (E, the money-flow tilt core moving beyond pure smoothing) scores novelty 3 and soundness 3; seeds 11 and 12 are struck, 11 seeds remain, and it passes. Slot b (N, overnight-versus-intraday tug of war) scores novelty 4 and soundness 4; seeds 7 and 8 are struck, 12 seeds remain, and it passes. R group 1 (+0.61, smoothing / denominator / slice variants) scores soundness 3 and passes. R group 2 (+1.22) is a real rewrite, not a rewording of the same content. Following my last audit, it replaces the volume-level power denominator with scale-free versions: Amt-weighted realized skewness (v1), ACJV skewness times the Amt z-score (v2), and the two combined (v3). That part really was bad: rho_known 0.58/0.52, float32 overflow with coverage 0.92, and a dose-response pattern. The variants do remove it: size exposure falls to 0.02–0.04, liquidity to 0.02–0.15, and correlation with the original head to 0.19–0.25. Soundness 3, passes. Not 4 for three reasons. First, the "bounded" claim holds only for v2; the day_wmean versions v1 and v3 are bounded by 1/√p, so a day where one low-money minute moves the price can reach about 69, and the 20-day mean is not trimmed, which is close to trap 3. Second, in v2, mul(skew, z) gives low-volume days a negative weight, so it tests the skew × abnormal-activity interaction, not "skew matters more when volume is low". Third, v1 has |ρ| 0.62 (raw) and 0.66 (residual) with the flow-tilt head +0.61, so it is closer to a relative of the tilt head.
